chosen_line.card: All Streams Flow to the Sea

q1_what_did_you_play: Both energy into damage, in a specific order: All Streams Flow to the Sea first, then Fathom the Tide, both at Nibbit. The order is the whole point. All Streams prints 11 'already including Charge', and the disclosure says it reads Charge at one point per two Charge, so its 11 is what 12 Charge buys; Fathom the Tide spends 6 of that Charge for its extra 6. Cast All Streams while Charge is still 12 and it is worth 11; cast it after Fathom and it is reading only 6 Charge, so it would be worth about 8. Played in this order I deal 11 + 13 = 24 and leave Nibbit at 16 with 6 Charge banked. Reversed it is 21. I eat the full 12, going to 36/70, which is never close to dangerous.
q2_other_line_considered: Two. The first was Fathom the Tide plus Coral Guard: 13 damage and 5 Block, so 7 through to face and Nibbit at 27. I rejected it because 5 Block against a 12 intent is not a wall, it is a discount, and buying 7 HP off a 48 HP pool with a card slot that could have been 11 damage is the wrong trade when nothing about this board threatens to kill me. The second was the Charge-conserving line, All Streams plus Water's Edge for 17, which leaves all 12 Charge intact so a future Fathom still has its full spend and All Streams keeps reading 11. That one I weighed properly, since Charge is a real resource and spending it now makes Fathom worse later, but 17 versus 24 is seven damage for a bank I have no printed reason to believe I need — nothing on this page tells me what a later turn looks like, and 24 now is the read I can actually justify from what is in front of me.
q3_what_it_gave_up: The 5 Block, so I take the attack whole: 12 to the face rather than 7. It gave up half the Charge pool — 12 down to 6 — which makes the next All Streams read 6 Charge instead of 12 and leaves Fathom's spend clause exactly on the line at 6. And it gave up Water's Edge and Coral Guard entirely, both unplayed at 2 energy. In exchange, Nibbit ends at 16, which is inside one more turn's reach.
q4_different_intent: Yes. The intent is what makes Coral Guard a rounding error here. At 12 incoming against 48 HP I can simply absorb it, so blocking buys nothing I need. Push the telegraph high enough that the hit threatens me — or start me low enough that 12 is a meaningful fraction of what is left — and Coral Guard stops being a wasted slot and starts being the card that keeps me alive to spend the banked Charge. A defensive or buffing telegraph would push the other way and make me even more comfortable dumping everything into damage. There is also a specific number that would flip the whole line: if Nibbit were low enough that 24 killed it, or if some line reached lethal that this one does not, the order and the card choice would be dictated by exact lethal instead of by max damage, and the Charge question would stop mattering at all.
